summary.headline: DEE Development Q2 FY27 revenue rose 8.5% to Rs 293 crore, EBITDA margin widened to 20.1%, order book reached Rs 2,531 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 293 crore (+8.5% YoY) with operating EBITDA of Rs 58.9 crore (+33.7% YoY, 20.1% margin vs 16.3%) and PAT of Rs 23.5 crore (+31.8%). H1 revenue was Rs 587.4 crore (+19%) and H1 EBITDA margin was 18.5% vs 16.2%. Management attributed the margin gain to Anjar and seamless pipe plant utilisation, a higher power-sector mix, and non-core tariffs, and cut finance costs after repaying Rs 225 crore of debt. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crore despite a slow H1 driven by job-work mix and GE HRSG orders not yet converted to POs.

segments.name: Piping and fitting (core)
segments.commentary: Power order book Rs 1,476 crore and oil and gas Rs 871 crore; power is over 60% of piping order book. Core piping and heavy fabrication anchor revenue and order book.

segments.name: Non-core (biomass pellets and Malwa power)
segments.commentary: 72,000 MTPA pellet plant at Muktsar ran its first near-full quarter in Q2; Malwa FY27 tariff Rs 5.44/kWh (under APTEL appeal). Management targets about Rs 80 crore non-core revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Seamless pipe (Anjar, 7,000 t)
segments.commentary: Plant now fully operational; output currently goes mainly to captive use, with some direct sales (e.g., an L&T pipe supply order). Management indicates about Rs 300 crore FY28 activity, split Rs 150-200 crore external and Rs 150-200 crore internal.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crore reaffirmed; management says about Rs 600 crore done in H1 and about Rs 750-900 crore net execution needed in H2 with WIP and RFP of Rs 100-125 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of about 19% reaffirmed; management argues fixed costs stay flat as revenue scales 40-50%.
FY28 order inflow expected above Rs 2,500 crore; FY28 revenue target of Rs 1,800 crore reaffirmed.
FY30 revenue ambition of Rs 2,500 crore; management says it excludes nuclear or new sectors.
Export mix guided above 50%; currently above 60%.
Inventory days guided to about 225-240 by year end (from 188 currently) against a 200-day working capital aim.
Nuclear revenue projected at Rs 50-60 crore in FY28 and up to Rs 200 crore in FY29.
Management expects H2 job-work share at about 30% and material contracts above 70%.
capex_capacity: Anjar fabrication facility and seamless pipe plant (7,000 t) ramping up; higher utilisation flowing through to numbers.
Seamless plant may need one or two more machines depending on inflow; two tenders (over 8,000 t) submitted.
Dedicated nuclear piping plant at Anjar, Gujarat under construction; machines ordered and being received.
Pellet plant (72,000 MTPA, Muktsar) expected to run both plants fully in H2; raw material bought for most of the year.
demand_pricing: Job-work share of H1 execution was about 40-45% (historically about 25-30%); job-work margins are 5-10 percentage points higher than full-material orders.
Order book includes GE LOI (about USD 40 million) but not Nooter frame agreement for Thailand plant (60% capacity reserved).
Siemens: two orders in last two to three months; minimum EUR 25-30 million FY28 business expected, mostly GT.
BHEL pending order about Rs 300 crore and L&T about Rs 150 crore; no Adani orders currently in book.
JSW and Adani large orders at advanced stage, expected December to February; one to be material-based.
October order inflow Rs 148 crore; order book Rs 2,586 crore at 31 Oct 2026.
Nuclear framework agreement signed 16 Oct 2026 with a domestic EPC (shop-manufactured piping scope); JV talks with a global partner expected to close by end FY27.
Data-centre order from Germany is on hold; a large US automation player discussions possible back-to-back partnership.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,500 crore FY27 revenue guidance achievable, and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Rs 600 crore is done and Rs 750-900 crore remains; it is sure of Rs 1,500 crore and reaffirmed about 19% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why have BHEL and L&T large orders not materialised and when will GE HRSG POs come?
qa_highlights.answer: BHEL process is slow and L&T price finalisation is tough; GE has issued only an LOI for two units, with a formal PO expected within a month or two and execution in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the job-work vs material split in the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Over Rs 400 crore of the Rs 2,500 crore book is job work; H2 expected to be over 70% material.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seamless pipe plant expected to be fully utilised and at what scale in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects near-full utilisation, with about Rs 300 crore of activity (Rs 150-200 crore external, Rs 150-200 crore captive).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the non-core pellet business still loss-making and what is the nuclear timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says losses have dropped; pellet ramp was cautious due to offtake and monsoon moisture. Nuclear revenue expected Rs 50-60 crore in FY28 and up to Rs 200 crore in FY29, with ramp slow.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 revenue ramp be sufficient given October execution of about Rs 80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says execution moves faster from December; tonnage to rise about 20% while revenue rises 40-50% as high-value material orders dispatch.

risks_watch: H2 execution must average about Rs 150 crore per month against October's roughly Rs 80 crore to hit Rs 1,500 crore.
GE HRSG orders remain at LOI stage with no PO; HRSG volumes at risk from US gas-turbine capex slowdown concerns.
Large JSW and Adani orders have repeatedly slipped; one may be job work, not material.
Job-work share (40-45% in H1) depresses reported revenue; mix shift to material is key to growth.
Working capital: debtor days rose in Q2; inventory days guided to 225-240 by year-end.
Nuclear and seamless revenue are early-stage projections; management says nuclear takeoff is slow.
Management could not reconcile the non-core power revenue figure (Rs 13 crore in presentation vs about Rs 5 crore in segment data); to be revert.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on FY27 revenue and margin targets, repeatedly saying numbers are sure despite slow H1 and delayed GE POs. Evasive on specifics for BHEL, L&T, GE timelines and the non-core reconciliation, and deferred several analyst questions to later follow-up.
key_quotes: So, our net execution will be around Rs. 750 odd crore, which we are quite confident and not only confident, we are sure that we shall be achieving that magic number of Rs. 1,500 crores by the end of the year positively.
Whether we get few 100 crores, less order, I mean, we feel that it's not that important. Main importance is the execution and the customer satisfaction.
Our export is very well on track for above 60% even now.
Nothing will happen in Q3, Q4, because still we do not have any order from them officially.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 cr (about 17% growth on implied base, H1 at Rs 587 cr needs Rs 750-900 cr in H2) is reaffirmed with order book of Rs 2,531 cr (+94% YoY) and seamless pipe capacity ramping, but H1 execution skewed to job-work and large BHEL/L&T/GE orders are delayed or not yet converted to POs, so backing is partial.

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew 8.5% YoY to Rs 293 cr while EBITDA rose 33.7%, so profit growth is margin-led (power mix, Anjar/seamless utilisation, non-core tariffs) rather than volume; the brief states no discrete one-off item or low base in the year-ago quarter, and the job-work share (40-45%) is a mix headwind to revenue, not a one-off.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin was 18.5% vs 16.2% and management reaffirmed about 19% for FY27, citing fixed costs flat as revenue grows 40-50%, though job-work mix is about 40-45% in H1 and dilutes margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Nuclear piping plant at Anjar is under construction with machines ordered and being received, and the seamless plant may need one or two more machines with two tenders over 8,000 t submitted; seamless pipe is fully operational at 7,000 t with about Rs 300 crore FY28 activity targeted.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book is Rs 2,531 crore at 30 Sep (+94% YoY) and rose to Rs 2,586 crore at 31 Oct, with H1 order inflow Rs 1,179 crore (+97%), though H1 revenue growth was 19% and H2 needs a sharp ramp.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Seamless plant may need one or two more machines depending on inflow and two tenders over 8,000 t are submitted, but no firm capex amount or date was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue of Rs 1,500 crore, but H1 was only about Rs 587 crore and H2 needs Rs 750-900 crore, so an upgrade is not supported.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: October execution was about Rs 80 crore against the roughly Rs 150 crore per month needed, GE HRSG is only an LOI, and BHEL/L&T/JSW/Adani large orders have slipped repeatedly.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Nuclear piping revenue is projected at Rs 50-60 crore in FY28 and up to Rs 200 crore in FY29 after a framework agreement signed 16 Oct 2026, but the ramp is described as slow.

rows.label: JSW and Adani large orders at advanced stage
rows.why: Management expects JSW and Adani orders December to February, but these have slipped repeatedly and one may be job work rather than material.

rows.label: Inventory days to 225-240 by year end
rows.why: Inventory days are guided to rise from 188 to 225-240 by year end, against a 200-day working capital aim, and debtor days rose in Q2.

rows.label: Finance cost decline after Rs 225 crore debt repayment
rows.why: Finance costs fell to Rs 15.3 crore in Q2 from Rs 17.2 crore in Q1 after the Rs 225 crore repayment, which supports PAT (+31.8% YoY in Q2).

tone.note: Management was confident on the Rs 1,500 crore FY27 revenue guide and about 19% margin, but evasive on BHEL, L&T and GE timelines and deferred several questions; analysts pressed on the H2 execution ramp needed from October's roughly Rs 80 crore.
